extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on using data visualization and infographic techniques to support investigative reporting, from finding and validating data to designing clear, accessible, and ethical visuals that tell a story and engage audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Data Visualization and Infographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Visualization is the process of transforming data into visual representations such as charts, graphs, and maps. Infographics are visual representations of data which are created to tell a story or convey a message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data visualizations to present complex information in easier-to-understand formats (charts, graphs, maps). Use infographics to combine information from various sources and tell a coherent story—often with illustrations, photographs, and text—so the message is quickly and effectively communicated. Combine both techniques to uncover patterns and create compelling arguments supporting an investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding the Right Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Select data sets that are directly relevant to the story and contain contextual information to draw meaningful conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate candidate datasets for: Relevance (directly tied to the story questions), Quality (complete, accurate, up-to-date), Accessibility (available in usable form), and Format (compatible with the intended visualization). Sources to search include government records, industry reports, public datasets, and academic studies. The right data helps reveal patterns and identify areas for further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the accuracy of data visualizations and infographics used in investigative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the source of the data; validate using appropriate statistical methods (correlation, regression, etc.); double-check against independent sources; consult experts to identify issues. Avoid stale or erroneous data and correct discrepancies before publishing. Accuracy is essential to maintain credibility and avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifying Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the provenance and trustworthiness of the data sources used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm who collected the data and their credentials, be alert for potential bias or conflicts of interest, consider the context (political, cultural, environmental) in which data was collected, and ensure the dataset is current. Treat source verification as a core reporting task—not just a technical check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-Checking Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform additional checks on datasets to find errors, inconsistencies, or outliers before drawing conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare datasets with other sources (on-the-ground surveys, alternate records), run 'sanity checks' to identify extreme or implausible values, examine demographic/contextual factors to spot bias, and correct or annotate discrepancies. Especially with large datasets, take time to inspect for errors that could invalidate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designing for Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Design visuals so they are easy to understand and interpret quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify data by including only necessary elements; create a clear visual hierarchy (group similar elements, use color/contrast to highlight important info); use clear labels, titles, annotations; minimize text and rely on visual cues; test visuals with diverse audiences to confirm clarity. Consider interactive elements to let users explore without overwhelming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing the Right Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Select chart or map types that best suit the story and the structure of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from the story: e.g., use line charts for trends over time, bar charts to compare categories, maps for geographic patterns, scatter plots for relationships. Consider how each visualization supports the narrative and the audience’s ability to interpret it. Also attend to aesthetics—colors, fonts, layout—to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping It Simple
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the core message and avoid unnecessary complexity in visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow the data to the most important points, use clean/minimal design, limited color palette, concise text, and simple shapes. Avoid overloading visuals with too many variables or decorative elements. Test with users to ensure the message is immediately clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Make visualizations and infographics accessible to people with disabilities and varied devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colorblind-friendly palettes or high-contrast schemes; ensure text readability (recommendation: fonts at least ~16px, sans-serif for legibility); design responsively for mobile and different screen sizes; provide alternative formats (audio descriptions, text summaries, accessible PDFs). Accessibility expands reach and prevents exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Interactive Elements to Increase Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Add interactivity (sliders, rollovers, annotations) so readers can explore data in depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive features let users discover insights at their own pace and can deepen engagement. Use interactivity to reveal layers of context, allow filtering, or show changes over time. But ensure interactions are intuitive and do not obscure key findings; test usability across devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing Impact by Combining Techniques and Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine charts, maps, diagrams, and narrative elements to create a more comprehensive and compelling story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different visualization types provide different perspectives; use multiple complementary visuals to illustrate complexity. Incorporate storytelling elements (characters, scenes, dialogue) where appropriate to humanize data and increase memorability. Balance comprehensiveness with clarity to avoid overwhelming readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Use visuals to construct a clear narrative rather than only presenting raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the story you want to tell and design visuals that highlight key points and connections (people, events, causes). Use annotations and sequencing to guide the reader through the evidence that supports investigative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Your Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor visualization choices and presentation to the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the audience helps determine complexity, tone, interactivity level, and format. For general audiences, favor simpler visuals and explanatory context; for specialist audiences, more detailed charts and statistical nuance may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Right Tools and Stay Up To Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate tools for creating visuals and keep skills current with evolving technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tools that match your needs (spreadsheets/statistical software for analysis, visualization libraries or platforms for interactive work). Stay current with new techniques and platforms to make use of more effective or efficient methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have an Eye for Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply design principles (color, font, layout) to make visuals attractive and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (colour, fonts, spacing, alignment) affect comprehension and perceived credibility. Use consistent styling, appropriate contrast, and clean layouts. Design complements clarity—good aesthetics should not override accuracy or accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize Social Media to Increase Reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use visual assets to promote investigative work on social platforms and reach a wider audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear, shareable visuals that summarize main findings to drive engagement. Optimize sizes and formats for different platforms and include concise captions or calls-to-action to encourage sharing and deeper exploration of the full story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test, Test, Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate visualizations before publishing to ensure effectiveness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test visuals with a range of audiences for clarity and comprehension, check interactions across devices, and verify that visual encodings convey the intended message. Use testing to catch misinterpretation, usability issues, or technical bugs prior to release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Presentation / Avoid Misleading Visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of ethical implications and avoid manipulating or distorting data in visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use color, size, axis scales, or selective data omissions to mislead. Provide context and explanations to prevent misinterpretation. Treat visualizations as part of rigorous reporting; they should support truthful representation of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze Data Appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Use proper analytical methods to explore relationships, patterns, and significance in the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply statistical techniques where appropriate (regression, correlation, cluster analysis) to substantiate claims and uncover non-obvious patterns. Analysis should be documented and defensible; use visuals to illustrate analytic results, but retain methodological transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: Visuals Are Not a Substitute for Traditional Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Visuals augment investigative reporting but cannot replace in-depth research, interviews, and document review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data visualization as an additional layer of reporting to support findings. Continue to conduct interviews, examine records, and verify facts; rely on visuals to clarify and communicate evidence, not as the sole basis for claims.
